reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs with no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited text supports compliance: Section 9(b) contains genuine express Vendor warranties covering performance to industry standards (9(b)(ii)), freedom from errors materially affecting utility (9(b)(vi)), no viruses/malicious routines (9(b)(iv)) and compliance with applicable Laws (9(b)(ix)) — matching the preferred position's substantive scope.

Duration analysis is sound: the warranties are continuing 'now and throughout the Term' obligations, and the Term is a 1-year Initial Term with automatic 1-year renewals, so the effective coverage equals or exceeds the preferred 12-month/90-day windows; the deterministic period check is satisfied.

The Section 13 disclaimer is bracketed by 'Except as expressly set forth herein' and 'except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement,' so it does not swallow the express warranties and walk-away 'AS IS' territory is ruled out.

The absent repair/replace/refund sentence is properly noted rather than flagged: it is a sub-element short of preferred wording, and importing a Vendor-elected exclusive remedy would narrow the customer's existing general remedies, cure/termination right and warranty-breach indemnity — consistent with the instruction not to flag clauses that benefit our party.
